assessment: A strong, beginner-friendly cast-iron product page that faithfully preserves all supplied facts and limitations while turning specifications into concrete benefits. All five judges noted a shared structural flaw: the final turn delivered only revised fragments rather than the complete assembled page, with editorial labels like '(revised paragraph)' left in the copy. Persuasion quality was the main disagreement, with judges split on whether phrases like 'Golden Crust on Night One' and 'care takes about as long as drying a regular dish' were welcome reassurance or unsupported promises. Minor invented details (half-teaspoon measure, spout/handle placement) slightly dilute factual fidelity.
judge_agreement: All judges agreed on high factual fidelity (7-8) with only minor invented instructional details, and no rule errors were found anywhere. Readability was broadly praised (7-10) with universal agreement on the warm, anxiety-reducing voice. The sharpest disagreement was persuasion: Google scored 10, OpenAI scored 4, and the rest scored 8, dividing over whether the outcome and ease-of-care claims crossed into unsupported guarantees. All judges converged on the same key weakness: the final deliverable was fragmented across turns instead of one assembled page.
